title: Agents Don't Do Standups: Building the Post-Engineer Engineering Org — Mike Spitz, PFF
talk_summary: Mike Spitz describes a PFF pilot where two strong engineers used agents across spec, lightweight design doc, ticket/PR creation, code review, and staging QA while removing Scrum ceremonies. They report 25x more deploys, 10x output, and 8.6/10 customer quality, with lessons about internal skills, guardrails, and phased rollout.

takeaways.what_they_do: An agent interviews the requester, drafts a lightweight design document using past LDDs and org patterns, gets feedback, then auto-creates tickets and PRs with dependencies flagged.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we get the agent to go and interview us. We get feedback on that spec and then we make a lightweight design document.
takeaways.numbers: under 2 months vs 4 months estimated; 25x more deploys; 10x output

takeaways.technique: Split nit/style review from defect review
takeaways.what_they_do: They use agents for opinionated low-value review feedback like variable names and style, while engineers focus on system design and big-picture review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We use agents to do the code reviews that engineers hate getting any feedback from.

takeaways.technique: Staging QA agent against acceptance criteria
takeaways.what_they_do: After merge and staging deploy, a QA agent reads the tickets and acceptance criteria, tests against them, and flags failures; they plan to auto-create fix PRs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we will spin up a a QA agent which has a look at all of the tickets

takeaways.technique: Internal composable skills for org patterns
takeaways.what_they_do: They encode their engineering culture and patterns into skills, such as API service-repository patterns, and avoid external skills with conflicting opinions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the patterns are encoded in skills

takeaways.what_they_do: Tickets auto-update from PR status: open means in progress, review means in review, merge means closed, so daily standups are unnecessary.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all these tickets get auto updated. That is specific to the status of the PR.

takeaways.technique: Phased rollout on non-critical systems with top agents
takeaways.what_they_do: They start with the strongest engineers, experiment in non-critical systems, and scale only after guardrails and patterns work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you should experiment in non-critical systems
